newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: WTO head hails Mercosur, Brazil dispute mars summit.
newsitem.headline: WTO head hails Mercosur, Brazil dispute mars summit.

text.p: The Mercosur customs union was given the thumbs up by the head of the World Trade Organization Wednesday, but a trade dispute with Brazil took some of the shine off the bloc's successes so far.

"The Mercosur is very succesfull and from this point of view the dynamic that it could inject in the liberalisation process of this part of the world is extremely interesting for us in the multilateral system," Renato Ruggiero, the Director- General of the WTO, told Reuters.
Ruggiero added that the fact that he had been invited for the first time to attend a Mercosur summit showed the region's integration is compatible with strong trade with the rest of the world.

But as economy and foreign ministers from the young customs union met on the first day of the two-day summit in Asuncion, Brazil's introduction in March of measures restricting import financing of less than a year became the topic of the day.

Brazil's Finance Minister Pedro Malan said the exceptions granted to Mercosur partners on the restrictions would be extended to October 31 from the end of July but it still underlined a rift between Mercosur's giant and the smaller members, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay.

Malan said he did not think the measure had affected Mercosur trade. "In a little more than two months' operation of the exceptions...there has been a significant increase in intra-Mercosur trade," he said.
"Brazil's decision is not quite what we wanted but we understand it," Uruguay's Economy Minister, Alvaro Ramos Mosca said.
On Tuesday, Jorge Campbell, Argentina's undersecretary of trade, said the group should introduce a "new special regime" for Mercosur imports which would solve the issue.
However, on the larger issue of the expansion of Mercosur in Latin America a dynamic began to emerge.
"Once you create a succesfull process like Mercosur you will inevitably see that this will be the core of the process of a Latin American regional process," Ruggiero said.
Ruggiero said the integration of Mercosur, which was formed in 1991, was running at a much faster pace than Asia's ASEAN trade bloc.
Mercosur signed a free trade agreement with Chile last year and Bolivia got a similar deal recently.

Importantly, trade deals or associations with more Latin American countries will give the group more clout in the negotiations for an American Free Trade Area (AFTA), envisioned by 34 heads of states in a hemisphere-wide meeting in Miami in 1994.

"We are discussing formulas allowing for Chilean and Bolivian participation in the discussion of Mercosur's position in its international relations (with AFTA and the European Union)," Uruguay's Foreign Minister Miguel Angel Maidana said.
On Tuesday, diplomats said there was agreement on setting up a working group to firm up the bloc's common stance towards AFTA.

At the same time, at the presidents' meeting Thursday to round off the summit, it is expected that emphasis will be put on further expansion. In addition to the four Mercosur presidents, the leaders of Chile and Bolivia will also attend.
Link-ups or trade deals between Mercosur and Mexico and the Andean countries of Venezuela, Colombia and Ecuador are seen as the most likely.
